query_ground_truth.workflow_task: Create AI avatar promo videos using a HeyGen avatar and voice, prepare supporting media, attempt social publishing, send a support email for infrastructure issues, and read/update a booking schedule.
query_ground_truth.rationale: Attempting social publishing requires uploading the media container and subsequently publishing it on Instagram.

results.execution_guidance: IMPORTANT: Follow the recommended plan below. Extract steps before execution, adapt to your current context, execute sequentially with current_step parameter, and check known pitfalls to avoid errors.
recommended_plan_steps: [Optional (if publishing account identifier is unknown)] [Prerequisite]: Resolve the publish-capable account identifier using INSTAGRAM_GET_USER_INFO (needed for publish calls).

[Required (if container identifier is missing)] [Prerequisite]: Create a media container using INSTAGRAM_POST_IG_USER_MEDIA (single asset) or INSTAGRAM_CREATE_CAROUSEL_CONTAINER (multi-asset) and store response.data.id as the container identifier.
[Optional (if you publish frequently or in bulk)] [Prerequisite]: Preflight remaining quota using INSTAGRAM_GET_IG_USER_CONTENT_PUBLISHING_LIMIT (continue if unavailable but posting is urgent).
[Required] [Prerequisite]: Get explicit user confirmation immediately before the public/irreversible call using INSTAGRAM_POST_IG_USER_MEDIA_PUBLISH.
[Required] [Step]: Publish the container using INSTAGRAM_POST_IG_USER_MEDIA_PUBLISH (allow extra wait for processing when needed) and capture the published media identifier from response.data.id.
[Optional (for verification/link/metadata)] [Next Step]: Fetch the published object using INSTAGRAM_GET_IG_MEDIA (use the published media identifier; request needed fields such as a permalink).

[Fallback (if publish is throttled, returns an unusable/ambiguous id, or container processing fails)] [Fallback]: Back off and retry INSTAGRAM_POST_IG_USER_MEDIA_PUBLISH later for HTTP 403 limit errors; if the container is invalid/consumed, recreate it via INSTAGRAM_POST_IG_USER_MEDIA or INSTAGRAM_CREATE_CAROUSEL_CONTAINER then republish once; if still uncertain, locate the newest item via INSTAGRAM_GET_IG_USER_MEDIA and confirm via INSTAGRAM_GET_IG_MEDIA.
known_pitfalls: [INSTAGRAM_POST_IG_USER_MEDIA_PUBLISH] response.data.id is the published media identifier (not the input container id); some wrappers nest it under a results/response object.
[INSTAGRAM_POST_IG_USER_MEDIA_PUBLISH] Container identifiers are single-use; if the API indicates it was already used/consumed, you must create a new container before publishing again.
[INSTAGRAM_POST_IG_USER_MEDIA_PUBLISH] HTTP 403 with limit-related errors can persist on rapid retries—use backoff and verify via INSTAGRAM_GET_IG_USER_MEDIA before reattempting.
[INSTAGRAM_POST_IG_USER_MEDIA_PUBLISH] The publish result can be missing/redacted/placeholder; validate that the returned identifier is usable before calling INSTAGRAM_GET_IG_MEDIA.
[INSTAGRAM_POST_IG_USER_MEDIA] HTTP 400 can occur when the media URL is not directly retrievable or when required media fields are missing; fix the media input and recreate the container.

toolkit_connection_statuses.description: Instagram is a social media platform for sharing photos, videos, and stories. Only supports Instagram Business and Creator accounts, not Instagram Personal accounts.
toolkit_connection_statuses.status_message: No Active connection for toolkit=instagram. You MUST call COMPOSIO_MANAGE_CONNECTIONS (toolkit="instagram") to create a connection BEFORE executing any instagram tools.

INSTAGRAM_POST_IG_USER_MEDIA_PUBLISH.description: Tool to publish a media container to an Instagram Business account. This action automatically waits for the container to finish processing before publishing. Instagram enforces an account-specific content-publishing rate limit over a 24-hour moving window; the exact cap varies by account and should be read live via INSTAGRAM_GET_IG_USER_CONTENT_PUBLISHING_LIMIT before bulk publishing. The publishing process: 1. First, create a media container using INSTAGRAM_CREATE_MEDIA_CONTAINER 2. Call this action with the creation_id - it will automatically poll for FINISHED status 3. Once ready, the media is published and the published media ID is returned For videos/reels, processing may take 30-120 seconds. Images are typically instant.

ig_user_id.description: Instagram Business Account ID (numeric string) or 'me' for the authenticated user. This ID is returned by INSTAGRAM_GET_USER_INFO or similar actions. Do NOT pass bank account numbers, connection IDs, or other non-Instagram identifiers.

creation_id.description: Container ID returned by INSTAGRAM_CREATE_MEDIA_CONTAINER (numeric string). This is NOT the same as ig_user_id. Do NOT pass bank account numbers or other non-Instagram identifiers.

max_wait_seconds.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the container to reach FINISHED status before publishing. Images are typically ready instantly, but videos/reels commonly take 30-120 seconds to process. WARNING: Setting this to 0 skips all status checks and attempts immediate publish, which will fail with error 9007 if the container is still processing (common for videos). Only use 0 if you are certain the container is already in FINISHED status (rare - typically only after manually checking via INSTAGRAM_GET_POST_STATUS). For videos/reels, use at least 60 seconds (default) or higher (up to 300).

graph_api_version.description: Instagram Graph API version to use. Defaults to v21.0.

poll_interval_seconds.description: Interval in seconds between status checks while waiting for the container to be ready. Default is 3 seconds.

INSTAGRAM_POST_IG_USER_MEDIA.description: Tool to create a media container for Instagram posts. Use this to create a container for images, videos, Reels, or carousels. This is the first step in Instagram's two-step publishing process - after creating the container, use the media_publish endpoint to publish it.

caption.description: Caption text for the post. Use HTML URL encoding for hashtags (# becomes %23).

examples: A sunset over the ocean with a sailboat in the distance.
alt_text.description: Custom accessibility alt text for a single image or an image carousel child. Maximum 1,000 characters. Not supported for videos, Reels, Stories, or carousel parent containers.

children.description: For carousel posts - array of container IDs (2-10 items) from previously created media containers.

cover_url.description: For Reels - MUST be a valid HTTP/HTTPS URL pointing to a custom cover image that Meta can fetch. Query parameters, including signed CDN or object-storage URLs, are supported as long as the complete URL remains accessible while the container is processed. If both cover_url and thumb_offset are provided, cover_url takes precedence.

image_url.description: MUST be a valid HTTP/HTTPS URL pointing to a JPEG image file that Meta can fetch. Must start with 'http://' or 'https://' (e.g., 'https://example.com/image.jpg'). Query parameters, including signed CDN or object-storage URLs, are supported as long as the complete URL remains accessible to Meta while the container is processed. DO NOT pass image descriptions or text - only actual URLs are accepted. At least one of: image_url, image_file, video_url, video_file, or children must be provided.

x.description: Horizontal position of the tag (0.0=left, 1.0=right). REQUIRED for images, CANNOT be used with Reels.

y.description: Vertical position of the tag (0.0=top, 1.0=bottom). REQUIRED for images, CANNOT be used with Reels.

username.description: Instagram username to tag (without @ symbol). Must be a public Instagram account.

items.description:
Model representing a user tag for Instagram media.

User tags allow tagging public Instagram accounts in media posts.
For images: x and y coordinates are REQUIRED to specify tag position.
For Reels: only username is used; x and y coordinates CANNOT be included.

user_tags.description: Array of user tag objects for tagging public Instagram accounts. For images: x and y coordinates (0.0-1.0, from top-left) are REQUIRED. For Reels: only username is allowed; x/y coordinates CANNOT be used.

video_url.description: MUST be a valid HTTP/HTTPS URL pointing to a video or Reel MP4 file that Meta can fetch. Must start with 'http://' or 'https://' (e.g., 'https://example.com/video.mp4'). Query parameters, including signed CDN or object-storage URLs, are supported as long as the complete URL remains accessible to Meta while the container is processed. DO NOT pass video descriptions or text - only actual URLs are accepted. At least one of: image_url, image_file, video_url, video_file, or children must be provided. When using video_url alone, media_type will be automatically set to 'REELS' if not specified.

audio_name.description: For Reels - custom name for the audio track (default: 'Original Audio').

ig_user_id.description: The unique identifier of the Instagram Business account (IG User ID) to create media for. This must be an Instagram Business account.

name.description: The filename that will be used when uploading the file to the destination service

s3key.description: The S3 key of a publicly accessible file, typically returned from a previous download action that stored the file in S3. This key references an existing file that can be uploaded to another service.

mimetype.description: The MIME type of the file

image_file.description: Image file to upload. The file will be uploaded to a temporary public URL for Instagram to fetch. At least one of: image_url, image_file, video_url, video_file, or children must be provided.

media_type.description: Media type for the container. Valid values: 'REELS' (for video content), 'CAROUSEL' (for carousel posts with children), 'STORIES' (for story posts). When posting video content with video_url alone (no image_url), this will automatically default to 'REELS' if not specified. Note: 'VIDEO' is deprecated and no longer supported - use 'REELS' for all video content.

name.description: The filename that will be used when uploading the file to the destination service

s3key.description: The S3 key of a publicly accessible file, typically returned from a previous download action that stored the file in S3. This key references an existing file that can be uploaded to another service.

mimetype.description: The MIME type of the file

video_file.description: Video file to upload. The file will be uploaded to a temporary public URL for Instagram to fetch. At least one of: image_url, image_file, video_url, video_file, or children must be provided.

location_id.description: Facebook Page ID of a location to tag. The Page must have latitude/longitude data.

thumb_offset.description: For videos/Reels - millisecond offset for thumbnail frame (default: 0).

share_to_feed.description: For Reels - whether to share to both Feed and Reels tabs. Only applicable when media_type is REELS.

is_carousel_item.description: Indicates this container is part of a carousel. For carousels: create 2-10 individual containers, then create a parent carousel container with their IDs.

graph_api_version.description: Instagram Graph API version to use. Defaults to v21.0.

INSTAGRAM_GET_IG_MEDIA.description: Get a published Instagram Media object (photo, video, story, reel, or carousel). Use when you need to retrieve detailed information about a specific Instagram post including engagement metrics, caption, media URLs, and metadata. NOTE: This action is for published media only. For unpublished container IDs (from INSTAGRAM_CREATE_MEDIA_CONTAINER), use INSTAGRAM_GET_POST_STATUS to check status instead.

fields.description: Comma-separated list of fields to return. Supported: id, caption, comments_count, is_comment_enabled, like_count, media_type, media_url, media_product_type, legacy_instagram_media_id, owner, permalink, shortcode, thumbnail_url, timestamp, username, alt_text, is_ai_generated, is_shared_to_feed, media_audio_type, view_count, reposts_count, saved_count, shares_count, total_like_count, total_comments_count, total_views_count, children, comments. For nested fields use 'children{media_url,media_type}'. UNSUPPORTED (cause errors): tagged_users, user_tags, location, filter_name, latitude, longitude, text — use 'caption' not 'text'. For insights metrics use INSTAGRAM_GET_IG_MEDIA_INSIGHTS. Tagged-media retrieval is unavailable through this Instagram Login toolkit. A MediaBuilder error means the ID is an unpublished container — use INSTAGRAM_GET_POST_STATUS.

ig_media_id.description: The numeric ID of the Instagram media object from the Graph API (e.g., '17858625294504375'). IMPORTANT: This must be a numeric string, NOT an alphanumeric shortcode from instagram.com/p/<shortcode>/ URLs (e.g., 'DUTi4n4D9wg' is NOT valid). Obtain numeric IDs from INSTAGRAM_GET_IG_USER_MEDIA or similar endpoints. For unpublished container IDs, use INSTAGRAM_GET_POST_STATUS instead.
